arxiv-2011-08098.title: Distinct distances on non-ruled surfaces and between circles Thanks: This research project was done as part of the 2019 CUNY Combinatorics REU, supported by NSF awards DMS-1802059 and DMS-1851420.
arxiv-2011-08098.creator: Surya Mathialagan, Adam Sheffer
arxiv-2011-08098.description: Abstract We improve the current best bound for distinct distances on non-ruled algebraic surfaces in ℝ 3 \mathbb{R}^{3} . In particular, we show that n n points on such a surface span Ω ⁡ ( n 32 / 39 − ε ) \Omega\left(n^{32/39-{\varepsilon}}\right) distinct distances, for any ε > 0 {\varepsilon}>0 .

arxiv-2211-01994.title: lil Gym: Natural Language Visual Reasoning with Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2211-01994.creator: Anne Wu, Kianté Brantley, Noriyuki Kojima, Yoav Artzi
arxiv-2211-01994.description: Abstract We present lil Gym, a new benchmark for language-conditioned reinforcement learning in visual environments. lil Gym is based on 2,661 highly-compositional human-written natural language statements grounded in an interactive visual environment. We introduce a new approach for exact reward computation in every possible world state by annotating all statements with executable Python programs.

arxiv-2307-06083.description: Abstract The dineutron correlation is systematically studied in three different Borromean nuclei near the neutron dripline, 11 Li, 14 Be and 17 B, via the ( p , p ​ n ) (p,pn) knockout reaction measured at the RIBF facility in RIKEN.

arxiv-2308-16467.title: A Posteriori Analysis and Adaptive Algorithms for Blended Type Atomistic-to-Continuum Coupling with Higher-Order Finite Elements
arxiv-2308-16467.creator: Yangshuai Wang
arxiv-2308-16467.description: Abstract . The efficient and accurate simulation of material systems with defects using atomistic-to-continuum (a/c) coupling methods is a topic of considerable interest in the field of computational materials science. To achieve the desired balance between accuracy and computational efficiency, the use of a posteriori analysis and adaptive algorithms is critical.

arxiv-2401-08497.title: Battery-Swapping Multi-Agent System for Sustained Operation of Large Planetary Fleets
arxiv-2401-08497.creator: Ethan Holand, Jarrod Homer, Alex Storrer, Musheeera Khandeker, Ethan F. Muhlon, Maulik Patel, Ben-oni VainqueurDavid Antaki, Naomi Cooke, Chloe Wilson, Bahram Shafai, Nathaniel Hanson, Taşkın PadırNortheastern University - Institute for Experiential Robotics360 Huntington Ave,Boston, MA 02115 {holan
arxiv-2401-08497.description: Abstract We propose a novel, heterogeneous multi-agent architecture that miniaturizes rovers by outsourcing power generation to a central hub. By delegating power generation and distribution functions to this hub, the size, weight, power, and cost (SWAP-C) per rover are reduced, enabling efficient fleet scaling.

arxiv-2510-21716.title: When Robots Say No: Temporal Trust Recovery Through Explanation
arxiv-2510-21716.creator: Nicola Webb, Zijun Huang, Sanja Milivojevic, Chris Baber, Edmund R. Hunt
arxiv-2510-21716.description: Abstract Mobile robots with some degree of autonomy could deliver significant advantages in high-risk missions such as search and rescue and firefighting. Integrated into a human-robot team (HRT), robots could work effectively to help search hazardous buildings. User trust is a key enabler for HRT, but during a mission, trust can be damaged.

arxiv-2511-10793.title: Curved Worlds, Clear Boundaries: Generalizing Speech Deepfake Detection using Hyperbolic and Spherical Geometry Spaces
arxiv-2511-10793.creator: Farhan Sheth, Girish Mohd Mujtaba Akhtar, Muskaan Singh
arxiv-2511-10793.description: Abstract In this work, we address the challenge of generalizable audio deepfake detection (ADD) across diverse speech synthesis paradigms—including conventional text-to-speech (TTS) systems and modern diffusion or flow-matching (FM) based generators. Prior work has mostly targeted individual synthesis families and often fails to generalize across paradigms due to overfitting to generation-specific artifacts.

arxiv-2512-04210.title: Balancing Safety and Helpfulness in Healthcare AI Assistants through Iterative Preference Alignment
arxiv-2512-04210.creator: Huy Nghiem, Swetasudha Panda, Devashish Khatwani, Huy V. Nguyen, Krishnaram Kenthapadi, Hal Daumé III
arxiv-2512-04210.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used in healthcare, yet ensuring their safety and trustworthiness remains a barrier to deployment. Conversational medical assistants must avoid unsafe compliance without over-refusing benign queries. We present an iterative post-deployment alignment framework that applies Kahneman–Tversky Optimization (KTO) and Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) to refine models against domain-specific safety signals.

pmc-10738520.title: EFFECT OF COVID-19 PANDEMIC ON A BODY MASS INDEX OF OLDER AMERICANS: A REPEATED CROSS-SECTIONAL STUDY
pmc-10738520.creator: Krishna Sapkota, J Scott Brown, Jennifer Kinney
pmc-10738520.description: IntroductionThe COVID-19 pandemic resulted in greater social and physical isolation, potentially leading to changes in eating, physical activity, and health behaviors, which may increase BMI. This study explored whether body mass index (BMI) among middle-aged and older Americans has been affected by the pandemic.

pmc-11478234.title: Seagrass Meadows: Prospective Candidates for Bioactive Molecules
pmc-11478234.creator: Hazeena M Ameen, Ayona Jayadev, Geena Prasad, Deepa Indira Nair, Guoxu Ma
pmc-11478234.description: Seagrass meadows consist of angiosperms that thrive fully submerged in marine environments and form distinct ecosystems. They provide essential support for many organisms, acting as nursery grounds for species of economic importance. Beyond their ecological roles, seagrasses and their associated microbiomes are rich sources of bioactive compounds with the potential to address numerous human healthcare challenges.

pmc-12661084.title: How I Do It: Interprofessional Education and Radiation Therapy—Establishing Opportunities for Student Learning in the Workplace
pmc-12661084.creator: Melissa Higson, Sonya Morgan, Eileen McKinlay
pmc-12661084.description: Clinical workplaces such as hospitals are often keen to arrange interprofessional learning activities for students on clinical placements, but radiation therapy (RT) students are often overlooked because of a lack of awareness and understanding of their role in patient care.

pmc-12690761.creator: Haro Yakouba, Compaore J Asiel, Sanou Abdoulaye, Zoungrana Inoussa, Zabsonre D Sylvain, Kabre Abel
pmc-12690761.description: IntroductionTumors of the posterior cerebral fossa account for more than 50% of encephalic tumors in children. Their severity is mainly due to the small size of the posterior fossa, making their management a dreaded problem in countries with limited resources.

pmc-12735459.title: Maternal Eating Styles and Restrictive Feeding Practices: Indirect Effects Through Perceived Child Appetite and Weight Concern
pmc-12735459.creator: Carla Ugarte Pérez, Claudia Cruzat Mandich, Camila Oda-Montecinos, Fernanda Díaz Castrillón, Álvaro Quiñones Bergeret, Antonio Cepeda-Benito
pmc-12735459.description: Background: Parents play a central role in shaping children’s eating behaviors. While previous research has documented associations between parental attitudes and feeding practices, fewer studies have examined how mothers’ own eating styles may contribute to their perceptions of their children’s eating attitudes and behaviors and how these may influence subsequent feeding practices.

pmc-13480381.title: Deciphering the Potential Mechanism of Cordycepin in Alleviating Ulcerative Colitis via the AKT1 Signaling Pathway: An Integrated Approach Combining Network Pharmacology, Molecular Docking, and Experimental Validation
pmc-13480381.creator: Wenting Zhang, Minyan Qian, Wenwei Jiang, Jie Chen, Nan Hu, Jingting Jiang
pmc-13480381.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). AimGiven the limited availability of safe and effective treatments for inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), we applied an integrated network pharmacology approach to systematically map the targets and pathways of cordycepin, a bioactive compound from Cordyceps militaris, in experimental colitis.MethodsCordycepin was administered intraperitoneally during dextran sulfate sodium (DSS) exposure in mice, with efficacy evaluated by the disease activity index (DAI) and histopathological analysis.

pmc-13715997.title: Theoretical Framework for Predicting Dynamic Covalent Exchange Based on Proton Affinities and Proton‐Transfer Assistance
pmc-13715997.creator: Siebe Lekanne Deprez, Stefan J. D. Maessen, Angelina N. van Dam, Celine Nieuwland, Pascal Vermeeren, Anja R. A. Palmans, Célia Fonseca Guerra
pmc-13715997.description: We provide design principles for predicting bond exchange kinetics in acylsemicarbazide (ASC)‐based systems that can be applied to tuning the properties of dynamic networks. Because of their capability of dynamic and reversible bond dissociation, ASCs are promising motifs in the design of tunable dynamic covalent networks that combine mechanical robustness with reprocessability and stability.
